findings.location: docs/feature/iis-slack-replace-remove/acceptance.md ### S2, the new row crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/handlers/instance.rs :: the table of what the confirm and remove pages reach when they are only read (stimulus F554, expected F555)
findings.obligation: A row's stimulus and expected state an observation this slice can construct; the row's cited obligations are L6/F201 and L6/F202, both of them confirm-door cases.
findings.observation: The stimulus also states that 'the remove page is opened with an app saved' and the expected covers 'each of those openings'. This slice delivers no remove door: its declared handler change is the I-14 gate on the save door and the confirm door's GET and POST, and L6's remove-door case F203 is cited by no row in acceptance, which holds S1 and S2 only. The remove-page half of this row is therefore not constructible at this slice, and a crafter authoring the table from the row text meets a handler that does not exist. Non-blocking: the two cited cases are confirm-door only and are fully constructible once the confirm door ships, so craft has everything it needs.
findings.remediation: Narrow this row's stimulus and expected to the confirm door with a submission waiting and with none, which is exactly what L6/F201 and L6/F202 name; let the remove slice add its own row citing L6/F203 and extend the same table then. Leave the locator's name as it is if the table is meant to grow, or rename it to the confirm page for now.

Finding 1 (blocking) is discharged at the public port. The new scenario at instance-integration-setup.feature:801 'A rotation of the current app's own secret is saved at once while a workspace is connected' is the missing discriminating stimulus: Canzan Labs is connected to Slack through the saved app 6123456789012.7234567890123, and Priya re-submits that SAME client ID with a blank client secret and a new signing secret. It asserts three independent public observations - she reads 'Saved. Workspace admins can now choose Add to Slack.', she is on the instance integrations page which still reads 'Slack: set up here, app 6123456789012.7234567890123', and no Slack app is waiting for her confirmation. A gate keyed on the connected count alone, which the previous oracle passed in full, now fails this scenario twice over: the POST answers the confirm page instead of the saved message, and a pending row is left waiting. US-IIS-05 AC 1 / P1 / E3 can no longer be lost silently.

The new Then step carries a real falsifier and one shared constant. 'no Slack app is waiting for Priya's confirmation' (steps/feature_instance_integration_setup.rs:226) calls then_nothing_waiting (support/instance_integration_setup.rs:1088), which GETs the confirm door as Priya and refuses a success answer carrying both I-14 phrases of the WAITING constant at support line 975 ['is connected through the current Slack app', 'Save the new app?']. That is the same constant the positive confirm reads use at lines 994 and 1016, so the negative and the positive observations cannot drift apart. Its failure message states WHAT (a submission left waiting here), WHY (it asks her to confirm a change she already made, in words about workspaces that keep posting through the old app) and HOW (hold a submission only where it names an app other than the one in effect), and prints the answer. The absent-door case answers 404, which is not a success page, so the step is honest before the door exists and becomes load-bearing the moment it does.

Residual on F183's count, judged non-blocking and recorded rather than reopened. F183 names 'Rotate with 3 connected workspaces'; the public harness has exactly one workspace, so the cited scenario reads a connected count of 1, and row S2[9]'s handler table cites only L3/F180 and L3/F182, leaving the Rotate-with-3 cell with no cited observation. A gate that read both facts and diverted a rotation only at two or more connected workspaces would therefore pass the whole oracle. Three reasons it does not block: L3's own statement F179 makes the Rotate row count-independent ('a Rotate never reaches the confirm'), so the count-1 witness falsifies the clause the law states; the 78736ff review's remediation offered the public scenario or the table row explicitly as alternatives, and this is the alternative chosen; and the surviving implementation needs kind and count read together against the stated law rather than the plain count-only gate that the previous oracle admitted. Cheapest later hardening, advisory only: list L3/F183 in row S2[9]'s obligations, where count 3 is reachable.

Finding 2 (non-blocking) is discharged where the boundary is decidable. The new row S2[11] cites L4/F188 ('the holder confirms at the expiry instant: nothing applied') to 'crates/foundry-store/src/integrations/instance.rs :: the finite table of when a held Slack app may still be applied, run by the iis_instance_store target' - L4's own declared owner locator, exercised by the declared command 'cargo test -p foundry-store --test iis_instance_store'. It is constructible before craft: crates/foundry-store/tests/iis_instance_store.rs already fixes an instant far from the wall clock at line 114 'so a store that read now()' is caught, and already builds admins and Slack connections through its admin() and connection() fixtures, so the clock can be set exactly at the expiry instant. still_passes_if F553 names the weakening it refuses ('a table that set its clock a whole minute past the hold would still pass while leaving the fencepost unread'). The table is not yet authored; authoring it and observing it is a completion obligation of this slice, not a pre-craft prerequisite.

Finding 3 (non-blocking) is discharged by narrowing plus one new row, with nothing left over-claiming. The handoff diff shows row S2[1] ('The admin who submitted the other app saves it from the confirm page') dropped L6/F201 and row S2[6] ('A confirm with nothing submitted changes nothing') dropped L6/F202, each keeping only the L4 case its public observation actually carries (L4/F187, L4/F192). The new row S2[12] cites L6/F201 and L6/F202 to 'crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/handlers/instance.rs :: the table of what the confirm and remove pages reach when they are only read' - L6's own owner locator, where the law's declared reason F204 ('the two GET handlers reach only read methods, which the table and the capability set together decide') makes the config-version clause decidable. Its disposition note keeps the honest limit ('a handler that bumped the version through a write the table does not list would still pass it'), with the public rows observing the rows and the activity that such a write would also move. No declared L6 clause now claims coverage it does not have. L6's third case F203 (the remove door) is cited nowhere and belongs to the remove slice, which acceptance has not yet authored.

diagnostic: Accepted: the blocking defect of the 78736ff review is corrected and no new blocker is present. The new public scenario at instance-integration-setup.feature:801 submits the same client ID while a workspace is connected through that app and asserts the saved message, the integrations page still naming it, and nothing waiting on the confirm address - so the count-only gate that the previous oracle admitted now fails twice over and US-IIS-05 AC 1 / P1 / E3 cannot be lost silently; its new Then step reuses the one WAITING constant the positive confirm reads use, with a what/why/how message. The two non-blocking findings are discharged at the locators their law owns: L4/F188's expiry instant at the store table run by the existing iis_instance_store target, where the fixed-instant helper already exists, and L6/F201-F202 at the handler read table, with the two public rows narrowed to the L4 cases their observations actually carry, leaving no clause over-claiming coverage. RED reused from the root's run at this clean revision with its current comparison: 20 scenarios, 11 passed, the same nine confirm scenarios failing on public answers with zero parsing and zero hook errors; the added scenario is GREEN by design because it preserves already-shipped behaviour. Completion obligations retained: the store expiry-instant table and the handler read table must be authored and observed, and the nine confirm scenarios must reach GREEN. One non-blocking oracle finding stays open - the new handler-table row's stimulus also names the remove page, which this slice does not deliver; it does not veto craft. Recorded residual, advisory only: F183 names three connected workspaces while the public harness reaches one, and the handler table cites F180 and F182 only, so a gate reading kind and count together with a two-workspace threshold would still pass; L3's statement makes the Rotate row count-independent, and the earlier remediation offered this alternative explicitly. typesafe: unavailable (exit 3, key absent), so these classifications are reviewer-owned.
